recent_posts.title: ScyllaDB vs Memcached performance comparison and architectural tradeoffs
recent_posts.summary: ScyllaDB and Memcached were compared head-to-head in a collaborative vendor-neutral benchmark. Both systems maximized disk and network bandwidth under similar conditions, sustaining comparable performance overall. Memcached stored 65% more items in RAM and showed better latencies for individual requests, while ScyllaDB required data modeling changes (wide partitions) to saturate network throughput and showed better latencies for pipelined requests. Memcached's Extstore needed additional IO threads to saturate disk I/O. The comparison reveals architectural tradeoffs: Memcached excels with simple key-value models and pipelining, while ScyllaDB better supports complex data models, persistence, and distributed replication. Both solutions efficiently utilize hardware when properly configured.

recent_posts.title: Caching and Latency [Book Excerpt]
recent_posts.summary: Explores caching strategies for reducing latency in software systems. Covers when to use caching versus other techniques, explains cache-aside, read-through, write-through, and write-behind patterns, and discusses client-side and distributed caching approaches. Details trade-offs between data freshness, consistency, complexity, and access speed for each strategy.

recent_posts.title: P99 CONF 2025 Recap: Latency to LLMs
recent_posts.summary: A comprehensive recap of P99 CONF 2025 covering tail latency optimization, systems programming, and database performance. Key themes included taming P99 latency across various systems (PayPal, TigerBeetle), widespread Rust adoption for performance-critical rewrites (SQLite, ClickHouse, Neon), database innovations in ScyllaDB and others, advanced testing with deterministic simulation, eBPF-based observability tooling, and the emerging frontier of LLM inference optimization and vector search performance. The conference featured 60+ talks from engineers worldwide sharing real-world performance engineering experiences.

recent_posts.title: Inside the Database Internals Talks at P99 CONF 2025
recent_posts.summary: P99 CONF 2025 features extensive database internals talks covering performance optimization, architectural decisions, and engineering challenges. Sessions include ClickHouse's C++ to Rust migration, TigerBeetle's tail latency reduction, SQLite rewrite in Rust by Turso, ScyllaDB's flow control and vector search implementation, and innovative approaches to userspace scheduling, tiered storage, and B+ tree optimizations for sorted sets.

recent_posts.title: eBPF Tech Talks at P99 CONF 2025
recent_posts.summary: P99 CONF 2025 features three eBPF talks covering thread-level observability with xCapture v3, concurrency testing using custom Linux schedulers, and memory-efficient eBPF instrumentation in Pixie. Previous conference sessions explored eBPF applications including noisy neighbor detection at Netflix, scheduler tracing with ftrace, zero-overhead container networking with Netkit, and database performance analysis. The talks demonstrate practical implementations of eBPF for solving production challenges in multi-tenant environments, container networking, and system-level performance troubleshooting.

recent_posts.title: Better Async Rust Disk I/O
recent_posts.summary: Benchmarks comparing different async Rust I/O approaches for disk operations, focusing on tokio, io_uring via monoio, and a custom abstraction layer called Fusio. The analysis reveals that spawn_blocking with pread/write often provides sufficient performance for sequential writes and random reads, while io_uring's benefits require broader application cooperation to be fully realized. Testing was conducted on AWS EC2 using real-world scenarios including Parquet file operations.

recent_posts.title: How a hidden VPA rate limit caused cluster wide pod evictions
recent_posts.summary: A detailed incident report about how a misconfigured Vertical Pod Autoscaler (VPA) caused widespread pod evictions in a Kubernetes cluster. The issue stemmed from the VPA Admission Controller being throttled by low API rate limits, preventing it from properly annotating pods and causing the Updater to continuously evict them. The problem was resolved by increasing the kube-api-qps and kube-api-burst parameters, highlighting the importance of understanding component internals and monitoring webhook performance.

top_posts.title: Switching From C++ to Rust
top_posts.summary: Nikita Lapkov shares his experience transitioning from writing C++ to Rust. He highlights the benefits of Rust's memory safety, unified build system, concise and helpful compiler error messages, and powerful type system with features like generics and enums. Compared to C++, Rust offers a more pleasant and efficient developer experience.

top_posts.title: Coralogix achieves 349x faster queries migrating from PostgreSQL to ScyllaDB
top_posts.summary: Coralogix migrated their metadata store from PostgreSQL to ScyllaDB, achieving a 349x performance improvement by reducing query processing time from 30 seconds to 86 milliseconds. The migration involved redesigning data models for NoSQL, implementing bloom filter chunking strategies, and optimizing partition keys. Despite challenges with data modeling and EBS storage decisions, the team successfully deployed a 3-node ScyllaDB cluster handling 10K writes per second with sub-millisecond P99 latency, processing terabytes of Parquet metadata for their observability platform.

top_posts.title: Rust vs. Zig – and C++ and Mojo – for Systems Programming
top_posts.summary: At P99 CONF, a debate between Jarred Sumner, Pekka Enberg, and Glauber Costa on ThePrimeagen's Twitch stream explored the benefits and drawbacks of Rust and Zig for systems programming. Key points included Rust's memory safety and robust ecosystem, and Zig's low-level control and better interoperability with C. They also touched on Mojo's potential, particularly for machine learning, and agreed that both Rust and Zig offer significant advantages over older versions of C++.
